acceptance.output_evidence: WHAT THE FIXTURE CANNOT SHOW. The fixture VALIDATES against the contract, so everything the contract can express is exercised; what it cannot show is everything the contract does not constrain. (i) FONTS, the largest gap, and it changes the OUTPUT not just the layout: the fixture DECLARES three Lato weights with their licence ref and does not PACKAGE them, rendering through the fallback chain Segoe UI/Arial/sans-serif. Every glyph advance changes, so line breaks move, so page breaks move, so the page count can move (2 pages here for performance and 1 for analysis -- neither survives the swap as a prediction); THE CONTENT HASH CHANGES BY CONSTRUCTION because it covers each page's content stream and a different font emits different text-positioning operators, so the arm's VALUE is font-environment-specific while its PROPERTY is not; and a missing licensed face degrades SILENTLY -- a browser substitutes, nothing fails, and nothing in the PDF says which face a fallback used. (ii) THE PRINT ENTRY POINT is a shape, not a behaviour: the contract says {module, export_name} and the real one is a JS export the counterpart mounts and calls; THIS CELL NEVER INVOKES A JS ENTRY POINT AT ALL, substituting a named-slot HTML template with str.replace and no expression language, so whether the real entry point is synchronous, waits for data or fonts to settle, needs a viewport or media emulation, or can fail partially and still resolve -- the four questions a print surface usually gets wrong -- are none of them asked here. (iii) PAGE BREAKS are exercised but on a page that cannot really break: break-inside:avoid and break-before:page are present and, with fixture sections of two short paragraphs, NEVER FORCED, while the real certified sections carry tables and charts that span pages.  WHICH ARMS MUST RE-RUN AT THE SWAP: (a) because the content hash is font- and layout-dependent -- the VALUE moves and the equality property must be re-measured, not assumed; (f) because the narrative census reads the RENDERED TEXT and a real component could emit narrative content the fixture template has no slot for -- THE ARM MOST LIKELY TO ACTUALLY FAIL; (v0.11) for the same reason, three times, with the page counts moving; (g) because the raw digest and therefore the receipt id change with the bytes. NOT (b), (c), (d), (e) or (amend): they test the bundle, the network, the asset layer and the authorization wrapper, none of which reads a rendered document. AND ONE ARM THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET: nothing today REFUSES to serve an export rendered from the fixture, though is_fixture_package() makes the swap detectable.  WHERE THE RUNTIME'S FONTS MOVE THE HASH -- four ways, and this is not hypothetical for this cell because it is why the deployed function does not render at all (row W4-S9): (1) a different FALLBACK CHAIN resolves differently -- Segoe UI is a Windows face and a Linux container resolves to DejaVu or Liberation or nothing, with different glyphs and advances, and THE DOCUMENT STILL RENDERS AND STILL VALIDATES; (2) the ENGINE VERSION -- renderer_version names a FAMILY deliberately because the build is not pinnable from here, and a Chromium minor can change shaping, hyphenation and sub-pixel positioning; (3) HINTING/DPI/print-color-adjust, which interact with the page box and the media box IS in the content hash; (4) the LOCALE for anything the engine formats. WHAT THE HASH CERTIFIES, precisely: two renders IN ONE ENVIRONMENT of one frozen bundle produce one document. It does NOT certify that two environments agree, and a cross-environment claim needs the fonts packaged IN the render package and the engine pinned by digest -- neither of which exists today.  WHAT A RECEIPT READER CANNOT LEARN -- the contract is additionalProperties:false, so the list is closed, and a reader cannot learn: (1) WHAT WAS IN THE DOCUMENT (no sections, no account count, no date range -- two exports of completely different scopes produce receipts distinguishable only by their hashes); (2) WHETHER THE RENDER PACKAGE WAS THE FIXTURE OR THE REAL ONE -- the sharpest omission: package_is_fixture is computed and printed by the worker and there is NO FIELD IN THE CONTRACT TO PUT IT IN, so a fixture-rendered receipt is indistinguishable from a real-package one; (3) WHICH ASSETS WERE USED OR REFUSED -- the firm's own logo versus the Opal fallback is exactly the question a firm asks about its branded document, and the bundle answers it while the receipt only points at the bundle by hash; (4) WHETHER THE PERFORMANCE REVISION CHANGED -- arm (b)'s whole claim is a property of two BUNDLES, and from two receipts a rebrand and a recalculation look the same; (5) WHO AUTHORIZED IT OR UNDER WHAT SCOPE (deliberate -- a receipt is not an audit record -- but it means only the _authz trail answers 'was this person allowed to have this'); (6) WHAT validation_status:PASSED ACTUALLY CHECKED (the count is 0 whether it meant 'parses and has pages' or something stronger); (7) WHETHER THE BYTES STILL EXIST (the receipt is immutable and the object is not). THE HONEST SUMMARY: the receipt is a good POINTER and a poor DESCRIPTION, every gap is answerable from the BUNDLE which the receipt names by hash, so the missing piece is not a field -- it is that nothing in this round stores the bundle beside the artifact. OBSERVATION, ARMED, disarm 2.0.0_SA_COO~B.
